title: finding(core): record-title.test.ts still calls the record-key probe "step 3b"
body:
`packages/core/src/utils/__tests__/record-title.test.ts:133` carries the same stale
precedence number that objectui#6634 corrected in the module it tests.

## The site

```
packages/core/src/utils/__tests__/record-title.test.ts:132-133

    // No fields to derive from, but the record carries a standard `name` → the
    // record-level name probe (step 3b) resolves it (better than `Record #7`).
```

## Why `3b` is wrong here too

Same rung, same argument as objectui#6634. `record-title.ts` states its ADR-0079 ladder
four times over and every one of them numbers the type-aware derivation from
`objectDef.fields` as step `4`, with the `NAME_ISH_RECORD_KEYS` probe beneath it as `4b`:
the module docblock (`:37`), the resolver docblock (`:380` / `:381`), the
`deriveTitleField` docblock (`:279`, *"precedence step 4"*), and the branch comments
themselves (`:437` / `:442`). Step `3` is `objectDef.titleFormat` — a rendered template,
not a record-key probe.

This same test file already spells it `4b` twice, at `:150` (*"so step 4b answered it
identically"*) and at `:245` (*"name-ish by NEITHER step-4b rung"*). So the file
contradicts itself seventeen lines apart, which is exactly the shape objectui#6634
recorded for the module.

## Why it was not folded into that card

objectui#6634's fence is `packages/core/src/utils/record-title.ts` alone, and the card
asked explicitly for other citing sites to be reported rather than renumbered. PR #6842
fixes the module and lists this line as the one citing site that disagrees. Filed
unassigned rather than widened into that PR.

## The natural shape of the fix

PR #6842 adds `packages/core/src/utils/__tests__/record-title.stepNumbering.test.ts`, a
source-reading pin that checks every sub-step label in `record-title.ts` against the
number the file's own ladder gives the rung it sits under. That pin deliberately scans
only `record-title.ts`, which is why it is green today. Widening its scanned set to this
sibling test file would both fix and mechanically hold this line — one edit plus one path
in the pin's scan list.

Observation only. No behaviour change: the number lives in comment text and no assertion
reads it.

## Duplicate scan before filing

The repo-scoped REST read channel is live in this container (authenticated
`GET /repos/objectstack-ai/objectui/issues/6634` returned 200), so this went through REST
plus a local grep rather than a search endpoint. objectui#6634's own filing-time targeted
MCP `search_issues` already covered this file's step numbering and returned 8 hits with
objectui#6572 as its positive control; treating that as the established reading, only the
increment since was re-read here —
`GET /repos/.../issues?state=open&since=2026-08-28T06:54:38Z&per_page=100&sort=created`,
100 rows, locally grepped for `record-title` / `precedence step` / `3b` / `4b` /
`deriveFromRecordKeys`. The only issue in that set about this ladder is objectui#6634
itself; the other matches are unrelated PRs whose bodies happen to contain those short
strings. Nothing covers the test file's citation. Note the bound honestly: that listing
was capped at 100 rows, so it is a bounded increment read, not an exhaustive one.

Refs: objectui#6634 · PR #6842 · objectui#6572
